content.overview: Article 79 constitutes the Parliament of the Union: it consists of the President and two Houses — the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
content.glance: Parliament = President + Council of States (Rajya Sabha) + House of the People (Lok Sabha).
content.study:
Article 79:
‘There shall be a Parliament for the Union which shall consist of the President and two Houses to be known respectively as the Council of States and the House of the People.’

Structure:
- President is an integral part of Parliament (not merely an external executive). Bills become law only after Presidential assent (Arts 111, 368 as applicable).
- Bicameralism: Council of States (federal chamber / permanent House) and House of the People (directly elected popular chamber).

Related: composition (Arts 80–81), duration (Art 83), sessions (Art 85), officers (Arts 89–98), privileges (Art 105), legislative procedure (Arts 107–111).

Examination: state the three components; emphasise that the President is part of Parliament; name both Houses correctly (Council of States / House of the People).

sections.heading: Constitutional text
sections.body: There shall be a Parliament for the Union which shall consist of the President and two Houses to be known respectively as the Council of States and the House of the People.

sections.heading: Exam checkpoints
sections.body:
1. Parliament = President + RS + LS.
2. President is a constituent part of Parliament.
3. Official names: Council of States; House of the People.
4. Link to composition (80–81) and duration (83).

misconceptions.trap: Parliament means only the two Houses; the President is outside Parliament.
misconceptions.correction: Article 79 expressly includes the President as a constituent part of Parliament.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How is Parliament constituted under Article 79?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 79, there shall be a Parliament for the Union consisting of the President and two Houses — the Council of States and the House of the People. The President is an integral part of Parliament.

examTips: Always include the President as part of Parliament under Art 79.
